Header:
Date: Tue 2026-07-21
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (VP Product), Jordan Kim (CTO), Chris Lee (CEO), Aisha Rahman (VP Eng), Omar Diaz (Head of Operations), ~All staff (audio dial-in)

Summary: (auto) Quick leadership handover, outage retrospective, hiring signal, roadmap triage, ops actions.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right everyone, good afternoon, yeah um thanks for joining this shortened all-hands. We'll try to keep it tight — we have a couple key things to run through: leadership handover plan, the regional outage review from July 4th, and a small product/ops reprioritization for Q3.
[00:15] Chris Lee: Hey team, quick opening, I want to thank folks who burned the midnight oil on the outage and the follow-ups, really appreciate it. I'm going to be out for two weeks starting next Monday, so Maya will be taking point on day-to-day, but we'll still be reachable for strategic decisions.
[00:30] (murmurs)
[00:32] Maya Patel: Thanks Chris. Ok, handover is light touch — I will be the primary escalation for incidents, Jordan and Aisha remain on technical escalation, Omar will manage People Ops stuff and hiring signals. We'll post the interim RACI in the commons after this.
[00:50] Omar Diaz: Quick note on people: we need a hiring pause signal — exec agreed to pause non-critical headcount for Q3 to protect runway. People Ops will circulate an exceptions list and a short exceptions request template.
[01:05] Aisha Rahman: Clarifying — this is a pause, not a hiring freeze for critical roles (security, infra, SRE), right?
[01:10] Chris Lee: Correct. Critical ops and security hires are green, product experiments and marketing openings outside core motion are paused. We'll be conservative.
[01:20] Jordan Kim: On the outage: quick recap — on July 4th early morning we saw a regional scheduler bug plus a regression in the autoscaler heuristics leading to a cascade of overloaded hosts and degraded KV cache warmups. The immediate impact was increased tail latency and higher error rates for a subset of hosted clusters.
[01:40] (someone coughs)
[01:42] Maya Patel: There were also some customers experiencing cold-start token inflation — the prefix cache wasn't hit and we saw token per-request cost spike. I want to stress this is a reliability priority for Q3.
[01:55] Jordan Kim: We're classifying root cause as a combination of: scheduler regression (deploy 7.3.2), autoscaler misread of SRK metrics, and slow KV cache reseed after instance replacement. The ops team mitigated via emergency backoff rules and a targeted rollback.
[02:12] Aisha Rahman: The mitigation worked but we need permanent fixes — proposed action items: resilient autoscaler default profile, an improved health check for GPU serving pods, and a fast path for KV cache reseed using snapshotting. Jordan will lead the benchmark for reseed performance.
[02:30] Jordan Kim: Yep, I will run a bench and share numbers by EOD 7/30 — want to show cold, warm, and warmed-by-prefix cases, especially long-sequence runs where the cache pressure is visible.
[02:45] Maya Patel: There's a customer comms note going out tomorrow morning, draft will be in the incident channel. Omar, People Ops will sign off on the tone?
[02:52] Omar Diaz: Yep, we'll review. Also, please flag any legal or enterprise customers who need a bespoke note.
[03:00] (background chatter)
[03:10] Chris Lee: Shift to product: Q3 priorities — we need to prioritize reliability and cost optimization vs new exploratory features. The board asked for clearer unit economics improvement paths. So product is to trim experiments and focus on: latency SLOs across host types, KV/prefix cache improvements, and a beta for smarter batching suggestions in the console.
[03:30] Maya Patel: We're going to re-scope the roadmap: move low-value experiments into backlog and accelerate platform tickets. Aisha, can your team provide a list of top 10 reliability bugs and estimated effort by Friday?
[03:42] Aisha Rahman: We'll compile and include rough T-shirt sizing. Some of the items are deep kernel-level attention optimizations and those will need cycles.
[03:52] Jordan Kim: Note: quantization experiments will be deprioritized except where they directly provide immediate unit-cost wins for hosted customers.
[04:00] Speaker 6: (inaudible) question about Dedicated customers — will this change affect SLAs or pricing?
[04:06] Chris Lee: No SLA changes. Dedicated and Private customers keep current SLAs. Any capacity policy changes will be communicated directly. Pricing is not changing right now; it's about operational focus.
[04:18] Maya Patel: Ops cadence — new weekly ops sync for incident readiness starting next Wednesday, cross-functional invite will go out. Also a simulation runbook exercise for the SREs and platform engineers on Aug 4th.
[04:32] (agreement)
[04:35] Omar Diaz: For hiring pause, we will publish the exception process and a small committee will review requests. Headcount leads — submit by Friday.
[04:45] Maya Patel: Security/compliance — we have to keep momentum on SOC2 recert and the ISO pre-audit; Security will run a deeper Q/A town hall on Aug 12th for product and sales about controls and customer asks.
[05:00] Jordan Kim: A tiny technical note — some transcriptions call KV cache "kay-vee" which is fine but in internal docs please use K-V cache or kv-cache for clarity, our docs are inconsistent.
[05:12] Aisha Rahman: Also cross-team note: when we talk about autoscaler heuristics, please don't shorthand to "autoscale fix" in tickets — include the metric names and thresholds, it's made debugging easier.
[05:25] (crosstalk)
[05:28] Maya Patel: Ok quick fires — metrics: we saw a 2.1x cost delta for certain long-sequence customers during the outage window, we've flagged those customers for compensatory credit where appropriate.
[05:42] Chris Lee: On the board ask — they want to see a two-pronged approach: short-term mitigations to reduce tail latency and mid-term investments in compilation/kernel selection improvements. We will share a short deck with the board next week.
[05:58] Jordan Kim: For the kernel path, research will prototype two micro-optimizations and we will test them on the daily night bench.
[06:05] Speaker 7 (remote): Question: will the console show more proactive batching hints?
[06:12] Maya Patel: Yes, that's in the Q3 visible scope — basic suggestions first, then an opt-in advanced advisor feature in Q4.
[06:20] (pause)
[06:25] Aisha Rahman: Action items recap — I will own the top 10 bug list, Jordan owns KV cache bench, Omar owns hiring exceptions, Maya will publish the RACI 
[06:38] Maya Patel: We'll also run a mid-quarter product review with sales to align on messaging and demos.
[06:45] Chris Lee: Anything else from leadership? (silence) ok quick shoutout to infra and SRE; please rest if you can, I know it's been intense.
[06:55] (applause and virtual clapping)
[06:58] Maya Patel: We'll close — thanks everyone. Draft incident postmortem will be shared by EOD tomorrow. Reach out in the incident channel if you have questions.
[07:05] End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: audio mix had multiple remote mics, occasional overlap and some words mis-transcribed (product names like "dedicated" as "decade" in a section), proper nouns sometimes missing special characters.
